_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: log ORs against placebo B -0.5, C -0.8

agreement.claim: both engines report the same random-effects estimates and SEs, common-effect estimate, tau^2, Q and inconsistency Q
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0, including tau^2 = 0.0437 (the fixture's seed was chosen so that tau^2 > 0 and the estimator is exercised). Local R had netmeta 3.7.0; CI installs 3.6-1. harness/synthesis_examples.test.py checks the estimates are exactly consistent, that the network SE for C vs B (0.105) beats the direct-only SE (0.150), and that the estimator is unbiased over the seeds.

recovery.claim: the estimates are close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: The comparisons with placebo are separated from zero; C vs B (-0.3) is not, at 15 trials. Measured by harness/synthesis_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99 (MALLARD_SEEDS=100); CI reruns it on seeds 0 to 49 at the same order statistic (owner decisions E5, E6).
